Authors: Crosthwaite, P.
Title: Bridging the Research-Practice Divide for Data-Driven Learning: Introduction to the Volume
Abstract: The various uses of language corpora for language learning now span decades of research quickly approaching close to 1,000 published articles. The direct use of language corpora for learning - also known as data-driven learning (DDL, Johns, 1991) continues to gain prominence in corpus linguistics and computer-assisted language learning (CALL) research (Crosthwaite et al., 2022). We stand at the cusp of unprecedented access to ever more powerful tools and ever-increasing corpus sizes as we emerge from the post-COVID world into the era of generative AI (artificial intelligence) and large language models. Yet, ‘prototypical DDL’ (Pérez-Paredes, this volume) has still largely failed to gain acceptance beyond applied linguist-led, higher education-focused contexts, leaving a well-documented research-practice gap between those involved in this research and those outside of it (Chambers, 2019). In response, a concerted effort must be made by corpus linguists and DDL research to reach out beyond their confines to new audiences, while at the same time inviting those new audiences to provide feedback on our research. This is the aim of this volume - to promote meaningful discussion between established researchers, early career scholars and DDL practitioners in the field on DDL-related affordances, issues and future challenges. This introductory chapter further elaborates the aims and scope of the present volume, before introducing the main contributions and their discussants. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Tian, Z.; Wang, C.
Title: Introduction
Abstract: The rapid advancements in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) have transformed language education, evoking a mix of “concern, curiosity, fear, and hope all at once” (Warner, 2022). On the one hand, tools like ChatGPT provide unprecedented opportunities for personalized learning, enabling autonomous skill development while alleviating teacher workloads through content creation and assessment tools. On the other hand, issues such as academic integrity, ethical concerns, digital inequities, and accuracy limitations underscore the need for thoughtful and responsible integration. This book addresses these complexities by drawing on conceptual, empirical, and practical work across diverse contexts – including English as a Second Language (ESL), English as a Foreign Language (EFL), world language learning, and language teacher education programs – to support educators, researchers, curriculum developers, and policymakers in tackling the pressing questions posed by GenAI. Our aim is to cultivate critical AI literacy among educational stakeholders, fostering inclusive and equitable learning environments that uphold ethical standards and celebrate cultural and linguistic diversity. Ultimately, this volume serves as both a roadmap and a call to action, inspiring the language education community to harness GenAI in innovative, ethical, and impactful ways that address the diverse needs of today’s learners. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Toncelli, R.; Kostka, I.; McMartin-Miller, C.; Zhou, L.; Szelenyi, B.
Title: Charting New Waters: Exploring the Role of ChatGPT in Postsecondary Pathways Programs
Abstract: The chapter describes a project that explores the uses of ChatGPT to support English language learning. Specifically, the chapter focuses on undergraduate and graduate multilingual students in two pathways programs at a large urban university in the United States. The chapter first discusses the educational context and relevant literature about integrating ChatGPT into teaching. Next, the chapter describes a collaborative planning process developed to engage students in initial discussions about appropriate uses of artificial intelligence (AI) during five in-class activities. These activities utilize ChatGPT in a variety of ways, ranging from critical analysis of generated narratives and emails to story development support and simulating dialogue with authors. The chapter then describes the integration of ChatGPT into class activities, noting how it assists in fostering a student-centered approach and serves as a useful tool to support English language development. The authors found that students share both enthusiasm and concerns about pedagogical uses of ChatGPT. Drawing from these findings to offer practical guidance, the chapter includes strategies for building teacher and student critical AI literacy skills and offers suggestions for professional collaboration. Future uses of AI in English language teaching are also explored. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Choi, W.; Kim, N.; Yu, W.
Title: AI-Integrated English Language Teaching in K-12 Classrooms: Insights from South Korea
Abstract: South Korea is known for the fast development of information and communication technologies, the “fever” for English language, and active application of emerging technology in language education. Recently, the South Korean government announced plans to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into the K-12 curriculum by 2025. Accordingly, education researchers and English teachers in South Korea are exploring and implementing AI pilot programs, encompassing various fields of AI technology. A review of these pioneering efforts may provide insights for other global contexts. Moreover, for teachers not to be stuck to using specific company-made programs in language learning, teachers need to be aware of the affordances and issues of different types of AI technology for language education. This chapter reviews exemplary cases from recently published research articles on AI-integrated English language teaching and learning in South Korea and suggests a guideline for K-12 English language teachers in global contexts. We first review theoretical concepts used in the reviewed articles. Next, we summarize the characteristics and functions of three main types of AI-embedded tools – AI chatbots (e.g., PengTalk), generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT, DALL-E), and AI machine translation (e.g., Naver Papago) – and describe how they were applied in South Korean K-12 English classes. Then, we discuss the impact, strengths, limitations, and implications of using each of the three types of tools in K-12 English classrooms. Based on this review and discussion, we suggest four guiding principles for AI-integrated language teaching and learning for K-12 English language teachers. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Amgott, N.; Renfroe, D.
Title: Implementing AI Chatbots in L2 University Courses: Building Pragmatic Competence and Critical Digital Literacy
Abstract: With the recent explosion of ChatGPT, many higher educational institutions have encouraged second language (L2) educators to weigh the benefits and constraints of incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into the curriculum. Such measures may involve detailing ethical implications of using AI on assignments, contributing to instructor hesitancy to implement intelligent computer-assisted language learning (ICALL). Despite the powerful learning potential of chatbots for facilitating pragmatic competence, literature has provided scant practical pedagogical approaches for implementing current AI as chatbots with our students. In this pedagogical piece, we explore illustrative examples of how university language educators can implement AI chatbots (i.e., Lingostar, ChatGPT and Gemini) to promote critical digital literacy and pragmatic competence. We outline previous research on L2 chatbot learning and review the affordances and constraints of several AI chatbots before providing four illustrative lesson plans for university language learners to navigate competences learners struggle to develop: pragmatics and critical digital literacy. We target honorifics in Korean and French (including address forms, honorific verb infixes, and speech styles) as a pragmatic language feature through which speakers index their social positions relative to each other. The chapter concludes with a discussion of the limitations of such tools and the potential for promoting ethical use of AI chatbots for conversational practice. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Curricula; Students; 'current; Chatbots; Digital literacies; Educational institutions; Ethical implications; Intelligent computer-assisted language learning; Learning potential; Pedagogical approach; Second language; University course; Teaching

Authors: Lynn, C.; Sayılı-Hurley, S.
Title: Scaffolded Integration of ChatGPT to Promote Language and Culture Learning
Abstract: This chapter addresses the challenges of traditional language learning curricula in reflecting the complexities of contemporary society, including diversity, social justice, and the influence of artificial intelligence (AI). The authors argue that generative AI, while potentially exacerbating existing biases, also presents opportunities for innovative pedagogy that can meet these challenges. To that end, students must be supported in developing AI literacy to critically and ethically collaborate with AI. The study reports on the implementation of a multiliteracies-based learning sequence in a fourth-semester German course, in which ChatGPT was used as a learning and writing assistant. The findings highlight how the integration of AI tools in language learning activities can facilitate critical engagement with multimodal content, while also recognizing the limitations and ethical concerns associated with AI-generated outputs. By supporting the development of AI literacy educators can develop students’ ability to navigate the complexities of AI and at the same time foster a more inclusive and reflective approach to language education. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Curricula; Teaching; Artificial intelligence tools; Ethical concerns; Language education; Language learning; Learning Activity; Learning sequences; Multi-modal; Social justice; Students

Authors: Sawin, T.
Title: A Five-Ecosystem Approach to Generative AI in Language Classrooms
Abstract: Applying generative AI in language classes requires more of teachers and curriculum designers than mere proficiency with AI tools. Leo van Lier cautioned early on that “technology has much to offer” but only in “service of a sound pedagogy”, one keeping pedagogical considerations first, curricular considerations second, and technological considerations third. In van Lier’s ecological approach, technological tools must be evaluated within a rich ecosystem of learner processes, social expectations, and other technologies. AI fits easily within this ecological approach, affording learners play, agency, and abductive learning (hypothesis testing about puzzling phenomena). Yet for such affordances to outweigh fears—of isolated learners, inauthentic language, and unoriginal thought—designers must carefully consider the context surrounding any integration of AI. This chapter details five ecosystems of context surrounding any AI activity. These are: 1) the pedagogical—classroom processes AI augments (e.g., providing formative feedback, structuring pair-work, and identifying key vocabulary), 2) linguistic—aspects of language learnable via AI (e.g., collocations, sentence structure, spelling conventions, and pragmatic conventions), 3) acquisitional—elements of the acquisition process (e.g., metalinguistic awareness, input flooding, pattern induction, and investment in content), 4) technological—the other tools (e.g., screenshotting plus drawing tools, social annotation, and search engines) AI need interfaces with, and 5) sociocultural—stakeholders’ (e.g., parents, IT support, and administrators) ideologies about language learning (e.g., privacy, studenthood, standardness, and creativity). Each ecosystem is described with reference to example applications of AI to the language classroom. Finally, two case studies illustrate evaluating AI within all five ecosystems to best cultivate AI’s potential. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Abiotic; Biotic; Curricula; Affordances; Ecological approaches; Ecosystem approach; Formative feedbacks; Hypothesis testing; Puzzling phenomena; Sentence structures; Social expectations; Teachers'; Technological tools; Teaching

Authors: Godwin-Jones, R.
Title: Language Teacher Preparation for an AI World: A Human Ecological Perspective
Abstract: This chapter examines the changes in second language (L2) teaching and learning which are accompanying the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and services. To appreciate the affordances and limitations of integrating generative AI into language education, teachers and students will need to understand the nature of systems based on large language models. The statistical model used to generate output in such systems validates a usage-based model of language which emphasizes patterns and regularities over rules. However, AI systems have no real-world experience and can produce language that is contextually and socially inappropriate. To use AI tools effectively and ethically, learners will need to develop critical AI literacy. The complex interrelationship of learner, mentor, peers, and AI systems is best understood using a human ecological perspective that incorporates the dynamics of the mind-body-environment relationship in educational settings. Using AI tools in language learning is an emergent process in which there is active collaboration among human and nonhuman participants. AI integration will necessitate new approaches and methods that accommodate the changing ecology of an AI world. That calls for a relational pedagogy based on contextual technology use rather than on the attributes of a specific AI tool. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Students; Affordances; Artificial intelligence systems; Artificial intelligence tools; Education teachers; Intelligence services; Language education; Language model; Second language; Teacher preparation; Teaching and learning; Teaching

Authors: Back, M.; Kabulis, K.
Title: Modality or Authenticity?: The Role of Authentic versus AI-Generated Texts in Language Learner Engagement
Abstract: The introduction of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT has opened up new possibilities for language teaching, including its ability to generate texts on different topics and for different proficiency levels. While potentially helpful scaffolds for developing interpretive language skills, AI-generated texts have not yet been evaluated with respect to their impact on language learner engagement. Similarly, although research and policies cite the importance of using authentic texts in the classroom, few studies have examined the role of authentic versus “inauthentic” (e.g., AI-generated) texts in engaging learners. Therefore, in this mixed-methods, action research study we assess learner engagement around authentic and AI-generated texts in two intermediate L2 French secondary classrooms in the United States. Using data from a strategic classroom observation protocol and discussions with learners, we discover that modality, rather than text type, determined the level of engagement among these students, with significant differences found between written and audiovisual text types, rather than between AI-generated and authentic texts. Given these findings, we explore the notion of “authenticity” with regard to AI-generated texts, and discuss implications for learner engagement and the use of these texts in the language classroom. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Action research; Artificial intelligence tools; Interpretive languages; Mixed method; Observation protocol; Proficiency level; Research studies; Teaching

Authors: Fincham, N.X.; Alvarez, A.A.
Title: Using Large Language Models to Facilitate Oral Proficiency Interview Practice for English Language Learners
Abstract: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have led to the development of powerful Large Language Models (LLMs) such as the ones that constitute the GPT family. The latest iterations of GPT models encode a wide range of human knowledge directly extracted from extremely large text corpora during the training process. This knowledge is enhanced and fine-tuned with human feedback, providing these models with human-like conversational capabilities and contextual understanding. Such enhanced capacities hold promising potential in enhancing language learning through personalized experience and guidance. This chapter presents the development and evaluation of a GPT-based application that is designed to guide English language learners in structured oral interview practices to help learners prepare for the ACTFL Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI) test. By leveraging the capabilities of GPT models, this application is able to automatically generate a large number of human-like natural questions based on a few contextual prompts and provide a personalized conversational experience based on learners’ responses. The evaluation results based on data collected from twelve oral interview practice sessions show that LLMs can be utilized to provide a well-structured interview experience for learners at three predetermined proficiency levels (novice, intermediate, advanced). With effective prompting strategies, the AI can generate high-quality output in terms of coherence, correctness, naturalness, and appropriateness. Our findings also indicate that an LLM-based conversational AI system has the potential to help sustain language learners’ engagement in independent language learning and provide personally meaningful target language input. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Contextual understanding; English languages; Evaluation results; Human knowledge; Human like; Language learning; Language model; Proficiency level; Text corpora; Training process

Authors: Dos Santos, R.G.-J.
Title: Afterword I: Second Language Writing in an AI and Multilingual World
Abstract: Writing in all genres and in all languages is undergoing a significant transformation through the arrival of generative AI. AI systems like ChatGPT are able to generate texts that appear in their coherence, fluidity, and grammatical accuracy to have been created by competent human writers. That development has occurred in parallel with a growing recognition of the reality of multilingualism today across the globe, along with the realization in SLA (second language acquisition) theory that individual plurilingualism needs to be integrated into instruction (Byrnes, 2020). Both developments have been underway for some time. AI-powered writing assistance has been enabled through advances in machine learning, resulting in digital writing tools able to provide auto-completion and real-time spelling, grammar, and style suggestions and corrections (Godwin-Jones, 2022). Now AI systems can generate output on virtually any given subject in multiple languages and at any given length and proficiency level, while also enabling L2 (second language) learners to check the accuracy and stylistics of their own writing. At the same time, in applied linguistics there has been a growing recognition that monolingualism is the exception rather than the rule in human society (Ortega, 2017) and that we need to recognize in SLA the plurilingual nature of language learning (and of most individuals’ real lives). That has led to the practice of pedagogical translanguaging (Wei, 2018) in which a learner’s first language is not banned from instruction but rather is used as a mediating and scaffolding tool (Cenoz & Gorter, 2017). Translanguaging and generative AI have enabled and invited – although in quite different ways – new and alternative writing practices. These changes are explored from various perspectives in this volume, with the authors offering both theoretical explorations and practical pedagogical suggestions. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: AI systems; Auto completion; Completion time; Machine-learning; Multilingualism; Multiple languages; Real- time; Second language; Second language acquisition; Writing tools

Authors: Vinall, K.; Hellmich, E.
Title: Whose Words Are They?: Authorship in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: In this chapter, we draw on Pennycook to explore the construction of the author, from birth to death, from two predominant Western theoretical perspectives: the modern and the postmodern. This undertaking allows for the exploration and identification of how faultlines between these historically conflicting understandings of authorship are challenged or reinforced in the age of artificial intelligence (AI). Given the longstanding ubiquity of machine translation (MT) tool usage in the language classroom, this exploration centers machine translation platforms as a foundation from which to then consider the implications of these faultlines for other AI language tools, particularly emerging generative AI technologies. More specifically, we illustrate these faultlines with excerpts from our on-going research project into how MT and other artificial intelligence-driven language technologies impact the teaching and learning of world languages. Overall, the exploration reveals the limits of modernist assumptions of authorship and the potential contributions of a postmodern perspective to the development of critical approaches to the use of MT and generative AI technologies to support language learning. We conclude with implications that include and extend beyond the digital tools themselves, as the identified faultlines point to the need to engage with broader considerations of the act of writing, knowledge production in the language classroom, and supporting agentive uses of digital tools to engage with meaning-making processes. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Computational grammars; Generative adversarial networks; Artificial intelligence technologies; Critical approach; Digital tools; Language technology; Language tools; Machine translations; Teaching and learning; Technology impact; Tool usages; Translation tools; Reinforcement learning

Authors: Xu, W.; Tan, X.
Title: Blessing or cursing: Second language writing teachers’ perceptions of using ChatGPT in classrooms
Abstract: Second language (L2) writing teachers are caught off guard with the recent advancement of AI chatbot-powered tools, featured by OpenAI’s ChatGPT. To provide opportune support for L2 writing teachers, it is important to explore the status quo regarding how teachers perceive AI, what experiences and responses they have, and what attitudes they hold. In this study, we surveyed 122 L2 writing teachers, with a focus on higher educational institutions in the US, and interviewed 13 of them. The survey and interviews tap into these L2 writing teachers’ own experience with and knowledge of ChatGPT, their knowledge of students’ use of ChatGPT, their evaluation of these behaviors, and their attitudes toward the use of ChatGPT in writing classrooms. Findings reveal that a majority of L2 writing teachers have had experience with ChatGPT for various purposes, and they have clear conceptualizations of potential benefits (e.g., increasing linguistic input for L2 learners) and risks (e.g., reducing critical engagement with information) of their students’ uses of ChatGPT in classrooms. Ethically, the L2 writing teachers identify the difficulties in drawing a clear-cut line in distinguishing students’ ethical uses of ChatGPT from unethical usage. This study sheds light on the diverse ways in which ChatGPT is perceived in relation to teaching and learning and provides pedagogical implications for how L2 writing teachers can make the most out of the technological abundance that our time has to offer in a responsible and sustainable way. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Index Keywords: Students; Chatbots; Clear cuts; Cut lines; Educational institutions; Potential benefits; Second language; Status quo; Teachers'; Teachers' perceptions; Teaching and learning; Teaching

Authors: Sydorenko, T.; Dombi, J.; Agrawal, A.; Thorne, S.L.; Lee, J.I.; Tao, Y.
Title: SPOKEN DIALOGUE SYSTEMS AND CHATGPT FOR SECOND LANGUAGE PRAGMATICS RESEARCH
Abstract: This chapter describes two recent technologies, Spoken Dialogue Systems (SDSs) and ChatGPT, and their affordances and challenges for second language pragmatics research. Since role-play is a commonly used task in pragmatics research, we discuss ways that the two technologies can be used for administering a role-play task. While SDSs are unable to deviate from a pre-programmed dialogue structure and thus cannot accommodate participants’ linguistic creativity, they are nevertheless systematic and allow for comparisons across participants. ChatGPT, on the other hand, is similar to a human in being able to accommodate participants’ creativity. As such, SDSs lend themselves to administering closed role-plays, while ChatGPT can be used to collect open role-play data. Nevertheless, ChatGPT’s responses are not fully natural compared to human responses and most often violate Grice’s Maxim of Quantity (i.e., they are too verbose). Future directions, such as multimodality and modifying ChatGPT’s behavior via prompt architecture, are discussed. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Pribble, K.
Title: Leveraging Generative AI Chatbots to Assess Writing in the Russian Language Classroom: A Model Portfolio Assignment with Chatbot Feedback
Abstract: This chapter presents a model for using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) chatbots to create portfolio-style formative writing assessments to teach Russian as a Foreign Language (RFL). The chapter considers recent discussions surrounding both the risks and potential benefits of GAI for higher education. Taking these risks and benefits into account, the author proposes a portfolio assessment that leverages the affordances of GAI while also addressing its limitations. The proposed assessment uses GAI chatbots to generate immediate feedback and record student progress, thereby engaging students in a recursive feedback loop. Drawing on the principles of Self-Regulated Learning (SRL) and student-centered pedagogy, this method facilitates active learning and critical AI literacy. The assessment also reestablishes classroom trust by offering transparent policies for the ethical and effective use of AI. The chapter concludes by reflecting on the author’s experience implementing this style of writing assessment in two spring 2024 Elementary and Intermediate Russian language classes and calling for future empirical research studies to validate the effectiveness and generalizability of this approach. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Pastushenkov, D.; Zalaltdinova, L.
Title: Assessment in Russian as a Foreign Language: Current Approaches, Emerging Trends, and Future Directions
Abstract: Despite its critical role in the classroom, Russian language assessment, along with many aspects of teaching Russian as a Foreign Language (RFL), remains under-researched. This review chapter introduces Assessment of Russian as a Foreign Language: Unlocking Proficiency, part of the Routledge Russian Language Pedagogy and Research series, which seeks to bridge the gap between research and practice. The chapter examines current approaches, including learner-centered and proficiency-oriented assessment, as well as technological advances, such as the use of lexical lists in automated proficiency assessment and the adoption of a constructionist approach utilizing the online Russian Constructicon. Emerging trends are also discussed, including developments in social justice (feminist assessment, ungrading), positive psychology (authorized cheat sheets), and technological integration, such as generative AI, “time capsules” for self-assessment, game-based assessments, and language learning apps. This review incorporates both quantitative and qualitative research, alongside pedagogically focused work, reflecting a shift from traditional to more innovative, humanistic approaches that link assessment and learning. Given the challenges in FL education, such as declining enrollment, supporting students through effective, learner-centered, and research-based practices is essential. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Xu, S.; Sun, Y.; Su, Y.; Liu, K.
Title: Translation Pedagogy in the AI Era: Design and Application of a ChatGPT-Powered Platform for Training and Feedback
Abstract: This chapter explores the design and application of an innovative AI-powered translation platform that integrates ChatGPT for translation training and feedback. The platform combines translation, post-editing, and evaluation functions to create a comprehensive learning environment. A theoretical background contextualizes the work within current AI applications in translation and language learning. The chapter details the platform’s design, highlighting its user and administrator interfaces, and discusses its potential applications in translation teaching and research. A pilot study provides empirical insights into students’ engagement with ChatGPT-generated feedback, revealing both strengths and limitations of AI in translation pedagogy. The authors critically examine challenges, ethical considerations, and future directions for AI integration in translation education. This research contributes to the ongoing dialogue about AI’s role in translation studies and offers a practical framework for leveraging ChatGPT in translation pedagogy. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Abril, C.A.H.; Hà, T.A.
Title: Opportunities and challenges of using artificial intelligence in language education: Perspectives from Vietnam
Abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted language learning (AIALL) is becoming increasingly prevalent across all educational levels, particularly with the widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT. However, AIALL still faces controversies and constraints, particularly concerning ethical concerns and plagiarism. These issues pose new challenges for language educators, as identifying the real authors of tasks and evaluating learners’ actual performance can be difficult. Despite the growing body of research conducted in the Global North, studies in the Global South context remain limited. Therefore, this qualitative study aims to explore Vietnamese language teachers’ perceptions regarding the opportunities and challenges of using AIALL. The findings are presented in six categories: (1) the profile of AI users, (2) characteristics of AI, (3) advantages, (4) problems, (5) risks, and (6) solutions for implementing AI in language education. Implementing AI in language education has the potential to introduce new quality approaches to both learning and teaching processes in Vietnam. However, it is essential for education stakeholders to have access to training to develop their digital competence, enabling them to understand both the potential benefits and the risks and challenges associated with AIALL. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Hiasat, L.; Coombe, C.
Title: Unlocking the power of intercultural awareness and competence: Experiential activities for tertiary level students in the gulf
Abstract: The topic of cultural awareness and competence is not a new one. Discussions of this topic have been around since the 1920s. However, with the advent of many technological advancements in recent years including Generative AI and social media, it is incumbent to explore cultural awareness and competence and its impact on language classrooms anew. This chapter explores intercultural awareness and competence through the lens of three wellknown and wellresearched theories of culture; Worldview theory, Hofstede's dimensions, and the Knowledge Workx framework. In doing so, we critically review these theories and present what we feel are still valuable aspects of these works as well as present our perspectives on what components need to be included in future cultural awareness and competence frameworks. For those teachers who envision a resurgence of infusing intercultural awareness and competence frameworks teaching into their classrooms, we provide several experiential and competencybased activities that can be used both inside and outside the classroom in the Gulf and beyond. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Blasing, M.
Title: Pathways for engaging climate, energy, and sustainability in the Russian language classroom
Abstract: This chapter examines the ethical, linguistic, professional development, and program advocacy benefits that emerge from teaching topics in environmental sustainability in the Russian language classroom. Situated in the context of challenges facing foreign language programs in 2024 American higher education, the chapter considers how teaching sustainability concepts in Russian classes can support an educational advocacy strategy in the face of threats such as declining enrollments in the languages, the rise of generative AI, widespread legislative initiatives in state governments to eliminate DEI programs, and an acceleration of cuts to world languages and cultures programs, which are increasingly seen as expendable by higher education administrations. Building on recent innovations in teaching sustainability and environmental literacy in the broader field of world languages and cultures (de la Fuente, 2021; Melin, 2019), the author offers a roadmap for an intermediate-level Russian language unit that addresses topics such as sustainable cities and transportation; recycling and waste reduction; and environmentally conscious habits for daily life. Built around the UN Sustainable Development Goals framework, the lessons proposed here are designed to integrate easily into existing courses, empower instructors to engage in content-based instruction in STEM-adjacent fields, and to create opportunities for students to engage with their local communities and communities across the Russophone world. Teaching sustainability and climate literacy will help instructors of world languages and cultures continue to make the case for the critical role of foreign languages and intercultural competence training in higher education. Such cross-disciplinary integration will also support graduates as they enter professions that will require sustainability knowledge and skills to tackle the practical, economic, cultural, and technological challenges of global climate change. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Sokolik, M.
Title: Using Technology to Teach Difficult Grammar
Abstract: This chapter examines the transformative impact of technology on second language grammar instruction. With the proliferation of digital tools and resources, instructors and learners have access to a variety of innovative methods for understanding and practicing grammar concepts. The benefits and drawbacks of using technology in grammar instruction are examined, including increased engagement and autonomy for learners, as well as the potential for technology to introduce or reinforce incorrect usage. Ethical issues associated with using AI (artificial intelligence) and digital translation are also examined. Practical tips for integrating technology into grammar instruction include online grammar exercises, speech-to-text, ChatGPT, and other applications. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Jung, N.
Title: Large language models for Korean grammar and spelling corrections: Comparative evaluation of Bard, Bing, ChatGPT, CLOVA X, and Perplexity AI
Abstract: This chapter evaluates the efficacy of six large language models (LLMs) – Bard, Bing, ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, CLOVA X, and Perplexity AI – in correcting grammatical and spelling errors in Korean texts. Utilizing nine Korean texts containing 100 deliberate errors, the study measures the accuracy of each model in error correction. The findings reveal that while ChatGPT-4 and CLOVA X demonstrate superior performance, there is a notable variety in the responses of these LLMs. The study identifies limitations of current LLMs, including instances of inaccuracies and the necessity for specific prompts to obtain accurate responses. It sheds light on the evolving nature of LLMs and their significant role in language learning, especially in providing immediate feedback crucial for enhancing writing skills. The chapter also raises concerns about the appropriateness of vocabulary for different learner levels and the variability in LLM responses. Advocating for an integrated learning approach, the findings suggest combining LLMs with human instruction to leverage the strengths of both AI and human expertise, thereby fostering a more balanced educational environment. The research underscores the importance of a thoughtful integration of LLMs into language education, acknowledging their potential benefits and current limitations while anticipating future advancements. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Kim, K.
Title: The potential of generative AI in writing feedback for Korean L2 learners: An analysis on grammar error correction by ChatGPT-3.5 for TOPIK II writing tasks
Abstract: The introduction and rapid expansion of generative AI technologies mark a significant advancement in L2 language education. Specifically, the application of conversational AI chatbots, exemplified by OpenAI’s ChatGPT, demonstrates considerable promise in the realm of L2 writing education. A distinct benefit of such technology is its ability to deliver high grammatical precision, providing essential insights into grammatical structures and writing formats crucial for L2 learners not yet adept in Korean writing practices. This interaction significantly contributes to learners’ ability to refine their writing skills and enhance their understanding of formality. This study is dedicated to investigating the potential of generative AI platforms in administering writing tasks. It utilizes practice tasks undertaken by students for TOPIK writing as the foundational material, employing ChatGPT’s correction functionality to produce improved writing samples. Through a meticulous analysis of these outcomes, this research seeks to unearth the capabilities of chatbots in the formal dimension of writing instruction and examine their utility in advancing the writing competencies of L2 Korean learners. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Chirciu, A.R.; Wren, J.
Title: A balancing act?: Opportunities for using chatgpt along with teacher instruction in the english as a second language writing classroom
Abstract: This research paper investigates the opportunities and challenges associated with integrating ChatGPT, a large language model, in the English as a Second Language (ESL) writing classroom. Grounded in action research principles, the study examines the effectiveness of ChatGPT as a personalized learning tool for reflection and action planning in writing. The research questions explore how ChatGPT assists students in their writing process, students' perceptions of its usage, and potential impacts on teachers' practice. The literature review discusses the rapid growth of AI technology in education, highlighting the benefits and challenges of incorporating ChatGPT in language learning. Empirical studies on ChatGPT's impact on writing skills and its use in the Gulf region are reviewed. The pilot study conducted with a class of Foundation Program students from Sultan Qaboos University employs student reflections and interviews as data collection instruments, analyzed thematically. The findings reveal that ChatGPT aids students in paragraph improvement, spelling and grammar correction, and idea generation. Students perceive ChatGPT as a valuable writing tool due to its convenience and specificity. However, limitations such as the lack of in-depth insights for academic writing and concerns about academic integrity are identified. The results contribute to the ongoing discourse on AI integration in education, emphasizing the need for pedagogical adjustments and clear policies. ChatGPT demonstrates potential as an effective tool for improving writing skills, necessitating further research to explore its long-term effects and develop guidelines for optimal implementation in writing instruction. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Can, T.; Mangır, C.
Title: Empowering Language Educators: Integrating Artificial Intelligence in Classrooms and Beyond
Abstract: This study seeks to evaluate the incorporation of ChatGPT, an AI-based tool, in developing instructional materials for language classrooms. Volunteer language instructors participated in a hands-on workshop led by industry professionals. A post-workshop survey evaluated the participants’ perspectives on ChatGPT’s usefulness and the likelihood of its future incorporation into instruction. The research also included an evaluation of instructional materials created with ChatGPT. Most participants viewed ChatGPT as an innovative and advantageous instrument for creating educational materials. Many educators are willing to implement ChatGPT in their classrooms. However, concerns regarding the implementation’s practicality and technical aspects were expressed. The study concludes that ChatGPT can potentially enhance the creation of instructional materials in foreign language classrooms. However, comprehensive training, ongoing support, and a focus on practical concerns are required for its successful incorporation into language instruction. This study contributes to a broader understanding of AI’s function in contemporary pedagogy by providing educators and policymakers with valuable insights on incorporating AI tools such as ChatGPT into education. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: Zerey, M.O.; Cephe, P.T.
Title: Exploring the Use of ChatGPT in Lesson Planning: Pre-Service Language Teachers’ Reflections
Abstract: ChatGPT, an artificial intelligence chatbot, might have transformational power for language teaching. One of the areas that might be of great benefit is the lesson planning stage, where learning objectives, teaching methods and techniques, materials, and assessment methods are clarified. The development of well-structured lesson plans requires profound knowledge and careful consideration. Therefore, pre-service language teachers who are in the process of learning how to develop lesson plans and implement them in their classes can use ChatGPT to support these endeavors. However, no study investigated pre-service language teachers’ use of and reflections on ChatGPT in the context of lesson planning. For this reason, this study aimed to explore the use of ChatGPT from pre-service language teachers’ perspective. This case study involved six participants who interacted with ChatGPT to receive feedback on their lesson plans that had been developed within the scope of a methodology course. The participants used this feedback to revise and refine their plans. Their experiences and reflections were investigated through semi-structured interviews. The data indicated that the pre-service teachers benefitted from the chatbot in exploring a variety of activities, revising learning outcomes, clarifying instructions, increasing student interaction, facilitating the planning process, and getting an external evaluation. These findings demonstrate the potential of ChatGPT as a valuable tool for pre-service language teachers to enhance their lesson-planning practices. In this sense, further exploration of ChatGPT in teacher education programs can contribute to pre-service language teachers’ professional development. © 2024 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
